The U.S. restricts exports of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to China but has approved some older models, and Huang has advocated for broader chip exports, according to CNBC.


## Lawmakers Seek Nov. 18 Huang Briefing After Nov. 17 Earnings


Three House Republican committee chairs have asked Huang to sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18, as reported by CNBC. Nvidia reports third-quarter earnings on Nov. 17 and will hold a major conference in Washington, D.C., at the end of the month, the outlet added.


## Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM): Taiex Rebounds as Much as 6.7%


Before Asian markets opened,[Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4668780-asian-stocks-face-new-pressure-as-nvidia-spy-probe-rattles-tech-sector) reported, citing Bloomberg News, that Asian equities faced renewed selling pressure as the investigation threatened to deepen a global technology stock downturn. Once trading began, equity-index futures for the[Nasdaq 100](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/nasdaq-100-how-the-index-works-and-who-gets-in/) dropped as much as 1% at the open after Nvidia's board announced the probe, according to Bloomberg.


Asian stocks followed Friday's US gains, Bloomberg reported. Taiwan's Taiex rose as much as 6.7% on Monday, with[Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/tsm/) and MediaTek each up at least 6%, per Bloomberg.


The rebound followed a steep sell-off last week. The S&P 500 posted its biggest weekly loss since April 2025, and $2.3 trillion was[wiped off the value of the Nasdaq 100 on Thursday](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nasdaq-record-point-loss-ai-stock-rout-wipes-25-trillion-us-futures-mixed-before-payrolls/) alone, according to Bloomberg.


"Asian markets are finding their feet again this morning as investors digest the rebound in US tech and the latest headlines around Nvidia's Jensen Huang," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade, per Bloomberg. Nvidia's board said it will provide further updates as appropriate.
